subject: Quantapay production: reserved-throughput shortfall and elevated latency (urgent)
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@quantapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@quantapay.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production impact: throughput below reserved, latency/error spike

Marissa / David,

Quick note from our ops team — starting ~07:00 UTC this morning our production traffic that runs on the Dedicated pool is seeing sustained QPS that is below what we reserved, but latency and 5xx error rates are spiking. Summary from our dashboards (attached CSV):
- Reserved QPS: 12k; observed sustained throughput: ~7.2k (60%)
- 5xx error rate jumped from ~0.4% baseline to 4.1% across multiple endpoints
- Median p95 latency rose from ~150ms to ~450ms for text-generation routes

This is customer-impacting for our checkout flows; retries are compounding the load. We need an immediate mitigation plan and visibility into whether this is a Redwood capacity reservation issue (throttle) or an internal client shift causing KV/cache misses.

Requesting:
- Immediate incident activation and an ops point (war-room)
- Short-term mitigations you can push (fallback model, burst/override, routing)
- ETA to stabilize and whether you can authorize a temporary burst + credit while we investigate

Attaching a small sample of traces and metrics. Happy to jump on a call — Ops is standing by.

Jordan Lee
Head of Engineering, QuantaPay
ops@quantapay.com

Attachment: recent_harvest_metrics.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@quantapay.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: throughput below reserved, latency/error spike

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We’ve kicked off a rapid triage. High level next steps were activating now:
1) Route new requests to a compatible lower-latency model variant (non-quantized) for the hot routes to reduce token-processing time.
2) Temporarily raise burst cap on your Dedicated pool for the next 60–120 minutes to absorb retry storms.
3) Enable relaxed per-tenant throttles (grace window) while we identify root cause.
4) Davids team will look into KV cache miss rates and recent prompt-size distribution (those are common causes of headroom loss).

Please send a few example request IDs and timestamps if possible (or drop them to this thread). Well update within 2 hours with confirmation of the temporary burst and the initial mitigation results.

For transparency: we will also document any one-off credits if we authorize a burst — will confirm the number as part of the next update.

— Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: service_topology.png
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@quantapay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: throughput below reserved, latency/error spike

Quick triage note from infra:
- Correlation shows a jump in long-sequence requests beginning 06:50 UTC. Average seq length for affected requests rose ~3x. That drives KV cache churn and increases per-token work.
- Cache miss rate on the shard serving QuantaPay increased to ~28% (baseline ~6%).
- No evidence of total cluster CPU/GPU OOMs; instead were seeing queueing at the inference front-end and increased tail latency due to KV shuffling.

Immediate actions pushed (in progress):
- Enabled temporary autoscale +1 GPU per shard for the next 2 hours (bump should show in ~5–7m).
- Activated fallback routing to a compatible model variant for short requests (cuts p95 by ~40% in local tests).
- Applied a quick per-client rate smoothing policy to reduce retry amplification (will throttle noisy spike generators by token-rate).

What we need from QuantaPay ops: 3–5 sample request IDs + approximate prompt sizes (to confirm client-side prompt growth). Also, confirm whether you recently rolled a client SDK change that might send bigger context windows.

Attachment: stderr_tail.txt
Technical owner: David Kim — david.kim@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production impact: throughput below reserved, latency/error spike — escalate to execs

Vivek — forwarding the thread. Davids triage points to client-side prompt-growth that combined with a retry storm has eroded the Dedicated pool headroom. We have temporary mitigations in place (autoscale bump + fallback routing) but QuantaPay is asking for an authorization for a short burst window and a potential credit.

Key facts:
- Observed throughput at ~60% of reserved for the last 45m with elevated 5xx and p95 latency
- Autoscale bump will buy ~2 hours of breathing room; fallback model cuts p95 by ~40% on short requests
- If we dont authorize burst/reserve override they will continue to see retries and user-facing failures

Request: can we get an exec decision to authorize a 2-hour burst (one-off) and provisional credit (20% of expected monthly invoice) contingent on joint post-mortem and remediation plan? If yes, please confirm and I will loop procurement & CS for credit note and customer comms.

Forwarded message below for context.

— Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@quantapay.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: throughput below reserved, latency/error spike

Thanks for the rapid triage and the clear ask. Im escalating this to the CTO and CFO now (copying them in the internal thread). Immediate decisions:
- Approve a 2-hour burst override for QuantaPay so their traffic can stabilize (Ops note: we will track metered usage and revert autoscale after 2 hours).
- Approve a provisional customer credit up to 20% of this months invoice, to be finalized after the post-mortem. Sales Ops to prepare the credit memo; Procurement + CS should confirm acceptance.

Next steps (owners):
- David: continue triage and send an incident note with root-cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline (by EOD PST).
- Marissa: coordinate credit memo and customer comms; ensure we schedule a joint post-mortem within 48 hours.
- CS / Account Ops: coordinate quota change, confirm burst has been applied, and validate customer traffic once stable.

Jordan — we will apply the burst now and send a confirmation once the change is live. Well follow up with the credit paperwork this afternoon. Appreciate the patience — well get this stabilized and share the remediation plan.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales & Partnerships (acting) | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
